strings.name: Mariana Mazzucato
strings.role: Economist · UCL professor of innovation and public value
strings.summary: Mazzucato studies innovation, public investment and value creation, arguing that governments can shape markets around explicit missions. She founded UCL’s Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose. Her books and policy advice stimulate debate about state capacity and sharing risks and rewards; practical outcomes depend on governance and implementation.

strings.influence.rationale: Studies innovation policy and state investment, developing mission-oriented policy and public-value analysis.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education

strings.highlights.h1.title: State and innovation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Highlights public institutions’ role in technological risk-taking and market shaping.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Mission-oriented policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Proposes organizing investment around social goals and sharing public risks and rewards.
strings.timeline.t1.title: The Common Good Economy published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Reconsidered economic cooperation and institutions through the common good.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Co-authored The Big Con
strings.timeline.t2.text: With Rosie Collington, examined consulting and governments’ internal capabilities.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Mission Economy published
strings.timeline.t3.text: Brought moonshot-style coordination into economic-policy debate.
strings.timeline.t4.title: The Value of Everything published
strings.timeline.t4.text: Examined distinctions between value creation and extraction and their policy implications.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Founded institute at UCL
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became professor of innovation and public value and founded IIPP.
strings.timeline.t6.title: The Entrepreneurial State published
strings.timeline.t6.text: Used public investment in innovation to challenge a purely market-failure view of government.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and Open University
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed her New School economics PhD and began a lectureship at the Open University.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Studied history and international relations at Tufts before turning to economics.
